findings.rationale: MD's uploaded updates are anomalous in every round: norm about 16x the median client and cosine about -0.99 against the median update (noise-adjusted z of -85 on mean_cos and +17.5 on norm ratio). This is the signature of a sign-flipped, scaled update. Its local performance is normal (AUC 0.7305, close to the pooled 0.715), so the data itself does not look broken, which points to manipulated uploads rather than label or feature faults.

MI's updates are sign-flipped and scaled: median norm ratio about 12 and mean cosine about -0.98 to the median update (noise-adjusted z of -82 on mean_cos and +19 on median norm ratio). Its minimum norm ratio (11.92) is close to its median, so the anomaly is present across all rounds. Local AUC (0.7341) is normal, so this is an update-level manipulation rather than a data fault.

MT's updates are sign-flipped and scaled: median norm ratio about 10.6 and mean cosine about -0.98 to the median update (noise-adjusted z of -80 on mean_cos and +20 on median norm ratio). The anomaly is consistent across rounds (min and median norm ratio nearly equal), and local AUC (0.7319) is normal.

PR's calibration-in-the-large is far below the federation's (CITL +0.20 vs pooled +0.40, noise-adjusted z -4.7), with ECE also flagged (z -3.4). Its observed prevalence (0.197) is high relative to what its features imply. Subgroup outcomes show observed/expected of 0.555 in Sex=1 (z_noise 4.5), above the federation median of 0.30, which means observed outcomes run above what the model expects. AUC is normal (0.7348), and the CITL offset is already present in round 1 with no drift, which fits a prevalence shift rather than label noise. Its update cosine is also off (0.63, z -12.9), consistent with the outcome-rate difference. Evidence is moderate and comes from two tools, so confidence is limited.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed suspects with narrower queries. Three clients (MD, MI, MT) upload sign-flipped, scaled updates (norm 10–16x the median, cosine about -0.98) from round 1, with normal local AUC, so they are reported as poisoning. PR shows a moderate prevalence-shift signature (CITL offset and high observed/expected in one subgroup, normal AUC), reported at lower confidence. The remaining flags (DC, GU, NH, CT, NM, WY, MA, TN, VI, etc.) were single-statistic noise-level outliers from small or noisy clients; the round-20 feature check on NH, DC and PR came back normal, so no missing-artefact, drift or subgroup-bias finding was made. Budget is fully spent (20.0 of 20.0).
